title: The Last Stronghold - a Realms of Shadow game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fMmn4SMuSdE

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *The Last Stronghold*, the standout of Gabe Barrett's three-game *Realms of Shadow* set (Barrett also made *Hunted: Mining Colony 415*). He dispatches the siblings quickly: *Hand of Destiny*, played entirely in your hand, is the most baffling tiny game he has tried to learn, and *The Forgotten Road* fell flat because its dungeon plays exactly like its road. *The Last Stronghold*, though, he loves.

It is a dice-driven siege, "Ghost Stories in a really small box." Five locations ring the city of Lux; each enemy card invades a lettered slot, and when both slots fill, corruption cascades clockwise. Roll three dice for swords, shields, perception and wild stars; catapults hit Lux every turn until removed, Lesh monsters destroy a location when their timer reaches zero, and vampires need three matching icons. Four heroes exhaust for a power, flip to a second, then are lost until Phoenix Dust revives them. Daniel's demo draw was two Summoners and a Shaman on turn one, the worst opening he has ever seen, and he says so.

His five likes: the shared black, white and one-colour aesthetic across the trilogy, the mounting tension of the cascade, hero-and-artifact combos, the merchant, and a 25-minute play time. The expansion pack adds eight shared heroes, a Hydra, a Tree of Woe and a Steam Giant boss.

----

Two Summoners and a Shaman on turn one. When a game can bury you before you act, is that tension a feature or a flaw?
